title: AI Music Streaming Fraudster Sentenced to 1.5 Years in Prison for $8M Royalties Scam
key_facts: Michael Smith, 54, was sentenced on Tuesday (6 Oct 2026) in Manhattan federal court to 18 months in prison plus two years of supervised release.
He pleaded guilty in March to using AI to generate thousands of songs and bots to stream them billions of times, earning more than $8 million in royalties.
It is the first criminal conviction over streaming fraud, Billboard says.
He agreed to forfeit more than $8 million; the charge carries a five-year maximum; guidelines called for 46 to 57 months; probation recommended 24.
His lawyers argued no victim suffered real harm; prosecutors sought at least 46 months.
The RIAA welcomed the ruling; the Music Fights Fraud Alliance said it would take 'more than one case' to stop streaming fraud.
quote_evidence: Michael Smith, 54, pleaded guilty in March to using AI to generate thousands of songs and then streaming them billions of times with bots, generating more than $8 million in royalties.
But at a hearing on Tuesday (Oct. 6) in Manhattan federal court, Judge John G. Koeltl ordered him to serve a year and a half in jail, followed by two years of supervised release.
why_it_matters_hint: The first jail sentence for AI streaming fraud sets a precedent, though shorter than guidelines suggested.
